description: Tamper rejection for the v0.5 `receipt` entry (§9.8): the sender recomputes receipt_sha256 from the receipt it RECEIVED (fixed-key/null wrapper) and reconstructs the context (in_reply_to top-level, `to` from its own drain identity). Receipts drive no action, but verification is a MUST — a fabricated or altered bounce could trick a sender into abandoning a live ask, and a flipped `prior` lies about whether the destination ever SAW the message (queued = never seen; delivered = seen-then-orphaned, §14.2) — exactly the false belief the delivery-honesty rules exist to kill. The honest control MUST verify first; each tampered variant MUST fail with a signature mismatch.
obligation: Verify the honest receipt (positive control), then reject every tampered variant with a signature mismatch: (1) `prior` flipped queued->delivered (the seen-ness lie — bound inside receipt_sha256); (2) `in_reply_to` rebound to a different message (rebinding a real bounce onto a live ask — bound top-level AND inside the digest); (3) `to` redirected to a different sender session (cross-destination replay — the reconstructed context diverges). Expected runner wiring (#26): mirror the dp-009 branch — rebuild the wrapper + context from each received receipt and verify against the fixture `v1`.

tampered_entries.reason: seen-ness lie — `prior` flipped queued->delivered: the sender would read never-seen mail as seen-then-orphaned; prior is bound inside receipt_sha256, so the recomputed digest diverges
correlation rebind — `in_reply_to` flipped to a different (live) message id: a real bounce for msg_01J5MSG0003 must not be replayable as a bounce for msg_01J5MSG0002
cross-destination replay — `to` redirected to a different session of the sender: a receipt signed for sess_01J5OVR0001's mailbox fails when the reconstructed drain identity is sess_01J5OVR0002
